planting.note: Plant divisions in rich, well-drained soil in light to deep shade; disturb the thick rootstock as little as possible once established, since growth is very slow.

directions: Grow in humus-rich, well-drained soil in light to deep shade, the same deep-shade niche favored by the straight species. 'Chirimen' takes its name from the crepe-like Japanese fabric it resembles, referring to the dense, fine puckering and rippling across the entire leaf surface rather than just the margins seen on many other textured selections. The tightly crinkled, dark green evergreen leaves hold their texture year-round and make the clump read as a distinct, fine-grained accent among smoother-leaved Rohdea cultivars. Offsets form slowly, so give it a permanent, undisturbed spot and expect only occasional divisions once the clump matures.
sources: Plant Delights Nursery / Juniper Level Botanic Garden

common_name: Night Light Sacred Lily (Glowing Variegated Omoto)

planting.note: Plant divisions in rich, well-drained soil in light to deep shade; the pale leaf streaking shows best where little direct sun reaches the foliage.

directions: Site in humus-rich, well-drained soil in light to deep shade, where the pale cream-to-white streaking down the center and along the veins of each leaf stands out against the darkest corners of a woodland bed. The name reflects how the bright variegation seems to catch and hold what little light reaches the plant, giving the clump a luminous quality in deep shade that solid-green Rohdea lack. Leaves are broad and leathery like the species, and the clump offsets slowly, so choose a permanent site and avoid repeated digging. As with most variegated Rohdea, some reversion to plainer green growth can occur on older offsets and can be removed if a uniform look is wanted.
sources: Plant Delights Nursery / Juniper Level Botanic Garden

planting.note: Plant divisions in rich, well-drained soil in light to deep shade; some bright indirect light helps hold the gold leaf margin, though the plant tolerates much darker sites.

directions: Grow in humus-rich, well-drained soil in light to deep shade; this selection belongs to the fukurin (margined) group of Rohdea cultivars, in which the variegation is confined to a consistent band along the leaf edge rather than scattered streaks through the blade. Each broad, leathery evergreen leaf carries a steady golden-yellow border around an otherwise deep green center, giving the clump a crisp, formal look distinct from the more freeform striping of many other Omoto selections. Growth is slow and offsetting like the species, so site it where it can remain undisturbed for years, and remove any all-green reversions if uniform variegation is the goal.
sources: Plant Delights Nursery / Juniper Level Botanic Garden
